concepts.title: Small and Large Families
concepts.description: Differentiating between different family sizes, specifically nuclear (small) families and joint (large) families.
key_ideas: A small family has parents and one or two children
A large or joint family includes grandparents, uncles, aunts, and cousins
Living together in one house

concepts.title: Our Family Name
concepts.description: Understanding that family members usually share a common last name, known as a surname.
key_ideas: Difference between first name and last name
The surname shows which family we belong to
Writing full names correctly

concepts.title: Fun with Family
concepts.description: Identifying activities that families do together to bond, celebrate, and relax.
key_ideas: Eating meals together
Celebrating festivals and birthdays
Going for picnics or outings
Spending time with grandparents

concepts.title: Respecting Our Elders
concepts.description: Learning appropriate behaviors and manners to show care and respect for older family members.
key_ideas: Greeting elders politely
Listening to what parents and grandparents say
Speaking softly and not shouting
Caring for elders when they are sick

concepts.title: The Five Sense Organs
concepts.description: Introduction to the five specific organs that help us perceive the world around us: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin.
key_ideas: Eyes help us see colors and shapes
Ears help us hear sounds
Nose helps us smell
Tongue helps us taste food
Skin helps us feel touch, heat, and cold

concepts.title: What Can My Body Do?
concepts.description: Understanding the specific actions and movements associated with different limbs and body parts.
key_ideas: Hands are used for holding, writing, and clapping
Legs and feet are used for walking, running, and jumping
The neck helps us turn our head from side to side
The mouth is used for speaking and eating

concepts.title: Correct Posture
concepts.description: Learning the correct way to position the body while sitting, standing, and walking to maintain a healthy spine and bones.
key_ideas: Standing straight with weight balanced
Sitting with a straight back against the chair
Walking with head up and shoulders back
Importance of posture for bone health

concepts.title: Growing Up
concepts.description: Recognizing that the human body grows and changes over time, transforming from a baby to a child and eventually an adult.
key_ideas: We are born as babies and grow into children
As we grow, our height and weight increase
Clothes and shoes become too small as we grow
We learn to do more things independently as we get older

Real-world applications of parts of a plant

concepts.title: What Plants Need to Grow
concepts.description: Introduction to the basic necessities required for a plant to stay alive and grow, emphasizing that plants are living things.
key_ideas: Plants are living things
Plants need water and sunlight
Plants need soil and air

concepts.title: Diversity in Leaves and Flowers
concepts.description: Observing and comparing the different shapes, sizes, colors, and textures of leaves and flowers found in the surroundings.
key_ideas: Leaves are mostly green but have different shapes
Flowers come in many colors and smells
Identifying common leaves (like mango or neem) and flowers (like rose or marigold)

concepts.title: Food We Get from Plants
concepts.description: Identifying the various types of food items humans consume that originate from plants, linking plant parts to the food on our plate.
key_ideas: Fruits and vegetables come from plants
We eat roots (carrots), leaves (spinach), and seeds (rice)
Plants provide healthy food

concepts.title: From Seed to Plant
concepts.description: A simple overview of the life cycle of a plant, explaining how a tiny seed grows into a baby plant.
key_ideas: Most plants grow from seeds
Baby plants are hidden inside seeds
A seed needs water and soil to open up

concepts.title: Taking Care of Plants
concepts.description: Learning the do's and don'ts of interacting with nature to ensure plants are protected and conserved.
key_ideas: We should water plants regularly
We should not pluck flowers or leaves unnecessarily
Trees give us shade and fresh air, so we must protect them

concepts.description: Homes of Animals — part of the chapter on Animals Around Us.

Real-world applications of homes of animals

concepts.title: Sounds Animals Make
concepts.description: Identification of the distinct sounds produced by common animals to communicate.
key_ideas: Different animals make different sounds
Common sounds: bark, meow, moo, roar, chirp
Listening to sounds helps identify animals even when we cannot see them

concepts.title: Young Ones of Animals
concepts.description: Learning the specific names given to the babies or offspring of different animals.
key_ideas: Baby animals often look like small versions of their parents
Specific names for babies (e.g., Dog-Puppy, Cat-Kitten, Cow-Calf)
Matching parent animals to their young ones

concepts.title: What Animals Eat
concepts.description: Introduction to the eating habits of animals, distinguishing between plant-eaters and those who eat other animals.
key_ideas: All animals need food to live and grow
Some animals eat grass, leaves, and vegetables
Some animals eat insects or other smaller animals
Some animals eat grains and nuts

concepts.title: How Animals Move
concepts.description: Observing and categorizing animals based on their primary mode of locomotion (land, water, or sky).
key_ideas: Animals use different body parts to move
Birds use wings to fly
Fish use fins to swim in water
Most land animals use legs to walk or run

concepts.title: Caring for Animals
concepts.description: Understanding the importance of kindness towards animals and basic responsibilities regarding pet care.
key_ideas: We should be kind and not tease or hurt animals
Pets need food, clean water, and a safe place to sleep
Sick animals need help from a doctor (vet)

concepts.title: Healthy Food and Junk Food
concepts.description: Healthy Food and Junk Food — part of the chapter on Food We Eat.
key_ideas: Core principles of healthy food and junk food
Step-by-step problem solving for healthy food and junk food
Real-world applications of healthy food and junk food

concepts.title: Where Does Our Food Come From?
concepts.description: Where Does Our Food Come From? — part of the chapter on Food We Eat.
key_ideas: Core principles of where does our food come from?
Step-by-step problem solving for where does our food come from?
Real-world applications of where does our food come from?

concepts.title: Why Do We Need Food?
concepts.description: Understanding the basic reasons why living things need to eat food to survive and thrive.
key_ideas: Food gives us energy to play and work
Food helps our body grow big and strong
Food protects us from falling sick

concepts.title: Meals of the Day
concepts.description: Identifying the three main meals eaten at specific times during the day.
key_ideas: Breakfast is the first meal we eat in the morning
Lunch is eaten in the afternoon
Dinner is the last meal we eat at night

concepts.title: Raw and Cooked Food
concepts.description: Distinguishing between foods that can be eaten raw and foods that must be cooked before eating.
key_ideas: Fruits and some vegetables like cucumber can be eaten raw
Rice, pulses, eggs, and meat must be cooked
Cooking makes food soft and tasty

concepts.title: Good Eating Habits
concepts.description: Learning and practicing good manners and hygiene related to eating.
key_ideas: Wash hands before and after every meal
Chew food properly and do not talk while eating
Do not waste food on your plate
Eat at a fixed time every day
